note: Reviewer-private verification harness. Production code is UNTOUCHED on this branch; the branch is based on the PR head (f8f2a59f) so the harness compiles natively, and the only additions are the pr418_*_test.go harness files and this docs/verification tree. Round 1 reviewed 8a54787d..f8f2a59f. IMPORTANT: the author force-added commit f8f2a59f ('Resume leaderworkerpattern cel validation') mid-review, which REVERSED the earlier design: the CRD default (+kubebuilder:default=LeaderOnly) was removed and the CEL rule restricting LeaderOnly to RoleInstanceSet roles was restored, with the LeaderOnly default moved into the controller (GetSharedServiceSelection). All findings below were re-derived against f8f2a59f, not the earlier 4811ab04. That change narrows the API surface but does NOT fix F1 -- it makes the guard unreachable for the defaulted path, because CEL only sees the stored object where the field is absent.

environment.sandbox: remote Linux sandbox root@43.99.38.217, go1.24.1, kubectl v1.36.2
environment.sharedInfraNote: An unrelated rbgs-controller-manager (2/2, image v0.8.0-47cfe17 == PRE-PR code) already runs in rbg-system on this cluster. The live layer deliberately exploits that: arm A records the CURRENT production behaviour via the installed controller, and arm B applies the selector PR#418 generates (proved at L1) as a SEPARATE Service over the same real pods, so no second controller is deployed and nothing cluster-scoped is touched. Everything lives in one throwaway namespace, deleted on exit.

integration.cmd: KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS=${KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS:-$(bin/setup-envtest use 1.31.0 --bin-dir bin -p path)} go test ./test/envtest/testcase/rbg/ -count=1 -timeout 20m -args -ginkgo.focus='PR418 F1' -ginkgo.json-report=$GINKGO_REPORT

liveNote: Needs a real cluster with the RBG CRDs and a running RBG controller ($KUBECONFIG honoured). The script creates one throwaway namespace, applies a StatefulSet-backed leaderWorkerPattern role with the policy unset, and compares endpoint counts between the selector the INSTALLED controller generates and the selector PR#418 generates. Expected signal on unfixed code: arm A > 0 endpoints and arm B == 0, plus NXDOMAIN for arm B's DNS name. Set KEEP=1 to keep the namespace for inspection. If the cluster's controller already contains the PR, arm A will also be 0 and the comparison loses its baseline -- run it against a pre-PR controller.

expectedAfterFix.F1: canary stays GREEN while the behaviour is accepted; flips if the narrowing is scoped to the RoleInstanceSet workload type, at which point invert or retire it
expectedAfterFix.F1b: canary stays RED under a selector-only fix; flips only if GetSharedServiceSelection stops returning LeaderOnly for workload types the CEL rule forbids it on -- invert or retire it then
expectedAfterFix.F2: canary stays GREEN while LeaderOnly remains the effective default; flips if the default is reverted or made explicit -- invert it then
expectedAfterFix.F5: canary stays GREEN (the worker binding under All is the intended behaviour); it exists to flag the upgrade rollout, so retire it once the rollout is documented
expectedAfterFix.F5b: stays GREEN; it pins correct behaviour and is worth keeping as a regression guard
expectedAfterFix.F3: canary stays GREEN until the RoleInstanceSet-level check also considers serviceName; the coverage gap closes when an All -> LeaderOnly case is added to the PR's own tests
expectedAfterFix.F6: closes when the PR adds its own StatefulSet + leaderWorkerPattern case
expectedAfterFix.F7: closes when the KEP is re-synced with f8f2a59f

F1.claim: A role with a leaderWorkerPattern pinned to the StatefulSet workload type, with sharedServiceSelection left unset, gets its shared headless Service selector narrowed to component-name=leader. No StatefulSet pod ever carries that label, so the Service loses every endpoint and its DNS name stops resolving.
F1.status: CONFIRMED as a defect, ACCEPTED on a deprecating path
F1.regressionProof: The same contract test PASSES at base 8a54787d (selector {group,role}) and FAILS at head f8f2a59f (selector {group,role,component-name=leader}) -- see results/l1-unit-base.txt. Live: 2 endpoint addresses -> 0, DNS NXDOMAIN.
F1.reachability: Only reachable by hand-writing the deprecated role-workload-type=apps/v1/StatefulSet annotation on a v1alpha2 role that also uses leaderWorkerPattern. The v1alpha1 conversion cannot produce that shape: api/workloads/v1alpha1/rolebasedgroup_conversion.go builds a LeaderWorkerPattern only when src.LeaderWorkerSet != nil, while StatefulSet falls through to StandalonePattern. The conversion code itself states 'New v1alpha2 RBGs should NOT set this annotation', and keps/workload-compatibility-mode/README.md deprecates the workload field. Downgraded from blocker to a TODO on the reviewer's guidance that StatefulSet is being deprecated; the evidence stands, the priority does not.
F1.polarityNote: Re-polarised from contract to canary once reachability was pinned down, so re-verify.sh does not report Still-broken forever for a consciously accepted behaviour. It flips if the narrowing is ever scoped to the supported workload type.
F1.dispositionChanged: Promoted from standalone TODO to the ENABLING change for a CRD default: the workload-type scope check is what makes CRD defaulting safe. Reachability is still nil in practice, so it remains low-urgency on its own -- but it is no longer optional if the default is made discoverable.

F1b.claim: The restored CEL rule rejects an EXPLICIT LeaderOnly on a non-RoleInstanceSet role, yet the controller applies exactly that policy to the same role through its in-process default. CEL cannot see the defaulted value because the field is absent from the stored object, so the guard is unreachable on the only path that matters.
F1b.evidence: results/l2-envtest-f1.txt -- a real API server refuses the explicit value ('only supported for RoleInstanceSet') and accepts the unset field on the very same role, after which the controller builds the leader-only selector.
F1b.canaryNote: Canary, not contract: scoping the SELECTOR to RoleInstanceSet roles (the fix that turns F1 green) does not change what GetSharedServiceSelection returns, so this test stays red under that fix by design. It flips only if the helper stops claiming LeaderOnly for workload types whose CEL rule forbids it.
F1b.note: Same deprecating path as F1, so same disposition. Worth recording because it is the root cause of F1: the API and the controller disagree about which workload types LeaderOnly applies to, and CEL structurally cannot close that gap for a controller-side default.
F1b.dispositionChanged: Same as F1: it is the evidence that the CEL rule cannot enforce the invariant.

F2.claim: For an existing RoleInstanceSet leaderWorkerPattern role that never set the field, the effective policy changes from all-pods (pre-PR) to LeaderOnly, so worker pod IPs silently drop out of the shared Service endpoints on controller upgrade with no user action and no change to the stored object.
F2.canaryNote: Whether LeaderOnly is the right default is a product decision, so the test records the NEW behaviour. Because f8f2a59f dropped the CRD default, the stored object keeps sharedServiceSelection absent -- so this change is now LESS discoverable than with a CRD default: nothing in the object tells an operator that leader-only selection is in force.
F2.askChanged: Revised: the ask is discoverability, not reversion. Keep the LeaderOnly default and restore a CRD default so the choice is recorded on the object, plus an upgrade note. The earlier framing ('keep nil -> All so the patch stays strictly additive') is superseded by the reviewer position above.
F2.severityNote: Still a silent behaviour change on upgrade, but corrective for the documented primary topology. Those actually hurt are users relying on the role-level headless Service for peer discovery over every Pod IP, which is a use the KEP never intended; they now need explicit All.

F5.claim: A role that already sets All gains a worker-component serviceName as a result of this PR. That rewrites the RoleInstanceSet template, and a serviceName change is classified not-in-place-updatable, so upgrading the controller alone replaces the worker pods of every existing All role.
F5.evidence: results/l1-unit-head.txt: worker serviceName == the shared service name at head; results/l1-unit-base.txt: the same assertion fails at base because the field is empty. F5b shows '' -> svc and svc -> '' both force ReCreate, while an unchanged value does not.
F5.canaryNote: Binding the worker under All is the intended fix; what needs review is the undocumented pod rollout it causes on upgrade. The KEP documents a rollout only for a user-initiated policy switch.
F5.raisedBy: Independently raised by @NoobDream2568 in a PR issue comment before this harness existed. This verification CONFIRMS it with evidence rather than restating it: the worker serviceName goes from "" (base) to the service name (head), and a serviceName change is classified not-in-place-updatable in both directions.
F5.releaseNote: Worth stating that the replacement is bounded by the role's rollout strategy rather than being a mass restart: limitUpdateIndexes caps concurrent updates at maxUnavailable in pkg/reconciler/roleinstanceset/statelessmode/sync/update.go, and statefulmode has an equivalent maxUnavailable budget.
F5.accepted: Accepted by the reviewer as a corrective rollout. No webhook or migration gate requested. Caveat carried from the discussion: do not assume the affected workloads were unusable -- anyone relying only on Service-level routing would have noticed nothing, yet their Pods are still replaced.

F3.claim: The reverse All -> LeaderOnly transition is untested, and the replacement guarantee it relies on is split across two layers of which only one knows about serviceName.
F3.status: CONFIRMED as a coverage gap (not a defect)
F3.evidence: results/l1-unit-head.txt: the RoleInstanceSet-level canNotInPlaceUpdate returns false for a serviceName-only change (with a passing size-change control proving the call is live). The pod-level isComponentExtensionSpecChanged is the only thing that forces replacement, so the documented rollout works -- but nothing exercises the reverse direction end-to-end.
F3.canaryNote: Agrees with Copilot's inline note on test/e2e/testcase/v1alpha2/shared_service_selection.go, and raises its importance: it is not a symmetry nit.

F4.claim: LeaderOnly is inert on LeaderWorkerSet roles with no signal to the user.
F4.evidence: The restored CEL rule now rejects an explicit LeaderOnly on LWS roles, which addresses the 'silently accepted' half. What remains is that the controller still resolves those roles to LeaderOnly internally (F1b) -- inert for LWS because reconcileHeadlessService is only called from sts_reconciler.go and roleinstanceset_reconciler.go, but not inert for StatefulSet roles, which is F1.

F6.claim: No test covers StatefulSet + leaderWorkerPattern, the combination where the policy actually misfires.
F6.evidence: The PR's own envtest adds an LWS case but no StatefulSet case; this harness supplies one and it fails.

F7.claim: The KEP still documents the CRD default that commit f8f2a59f removed, and no longer documents the CEL rule that f8f2a59f restored. Three concrete contradictions: the Go snippet still carries +kubebuilder:default=LeaderOnly; the Default section still says 'the API server defaults it to LeaderOnly'; and the '### Validation' section describing the CEL rule was deleted in 4811ab04 and never restored alongside the rule itself.
F7.evidence: git diff --name-only 4811ab04..f8f2a59f lists six files and keps/260-leaderonly-service/README.md is NOT among them, while the same commit removed the marker from api/workloads/v1alpha2/rolebasedgroup_types.go and restored the RoleSpec CEL rule.
F7.raisedBy: Raised by @NoobDream2568 on keps/260-leaderonly-service/README.md:179. The author replied 'You're probably seeing stale code. I've removed the default value...', which addresses the Go code but not the KEP the comment points at -- the KEP is genuinely still stale, so the comment was correct and remains unresolved.
F7.knockOn: IMPORTANT: the correct re-sync direction depends on the default decision. If the CRD default returns, the +kubebuilder:default marker and the 'the API server defaults it to LeaderOnly' line become CORRECT again, and what needs removing is instead the 'deliberately not a CRD default' comment f8f2a59f added to rolebasedgroup_types.go. The '### Validation' section should only be restored if the CEL rule stays. The author has already said 'Good catch. I'll go ahead and update the documentation' (diw-zw, 2026-08-07T03:54:54Z), so raising this before that work lands avoids a second revision.

reviewerPosition.default: Keep LeaderOnly as the effective default. The KEP's own motivation justifies it: the pre-PR all-Pods default routes requests at worker Pods that may only run a dummy API server, and all six leaderWorkerPattern examples in the repo leave the field unset, so the intended topology is exactly the mis-served one. LeaderOnly is corrective, not merely preferable.
reviewerPosition.asked: Make the default DISCOVERABLE. f8f2a59f keeps the CEL rule and moves the default into the controller, which is the worst combination for F2: the behaviour changes while nothing in the stored object records it -- no kubectl -o yaml evidence, nothing to diff or audit.
reviewerPosition.tension: A CRD default and the restored CEL rule are mutually exclusive, because defaulting runs before validation: a CRD default writes LeaderOnly onto every LWS/StatefulSet role and CEL then rejects it.
reviewerPosition.proposal: CRD default + drop the CEL rule + add role.GetWorkloadType() == RoleInstanceSetWorkloadType to the narrowing condition in svc_reconciler.go. F1b is the evidence that the CEL rule is the weaker piece: it blocks only the explicit spelling of a policy the controller applies anyway via the unset path, so it is ceremony rather than protection. The scope check enforces the real invariant and fixes F1 in passing.
reviewerPosition.notARevert: This is NOT a return to 4811ab04. That commit dropped the CEL rule WITHOUT the scope check, which is exactly what produced F1. Dropping it WITH the check is a different proposal.
reviewerPosition.residualCost: LeaderOnly becomes writable on LWS roles where it is inert. A documentation line covers it; a status condition exposing the effective policy would be more rigorous but is probably not worth the added surface.
